differential.name: Chronic kidney disease, hypertensive nephrosclerosis
differential.rationale: Markedly elevated creatinine (3.5 mg/dL) in a middle‑aged adult with hyperlipidemia and likely undiagnosed hypertension is most consistent with hypertensive CKD.

differential.name: Chronic kidney disease, diabetic nephropathy
differential.rationale: CKD presentation with high creatinine; diabetes not documented but is a common cause of CKD in this age group.

differential.name: Chronic kidney disease, obstructive uropathy (e.g., benign prostatic hyperplasia)
differential.rationale: Upper‑tract obstruction can produce a gradual rise in creatinine; male patients in their 50s often develop BPH‑related obstruction.

differential.name: Acute kidney injury superimposed on CKD due to NSAID use (acute tubular necrosis)
differential.rationale: Asthma patients frequently use NSAIDs; recent AKI can raise creatinine on top of chronic renal impairment.

differential.name: Chronic glomerulonephritis (IgA nephropathy)
differential.rationale: Glomerular disease can cause progressive CKD with modest proteinuria; fits a non‑diabetic, non‑hypertensive renal decline.
